thesis: A two-sided benefits and mobility payments network with ROIC rising to 18.5% and a 38.2% FCF margin trades at the bottom of its own 5-year multiples and below peers on P/E, where the price implies a revenue decline that reaffirmed guidance and 6.6% Q3 intrinsic growth do not show.
reason: Rising returns, strong cash generation and a price implying shrinkage against guided growth give a favourable skew. Unresolved Italy/Brazil voucher regulation, float-flattered FCF and a mechanical bear value below the price cap conviction at 4, not 5: standard volatility-scaled core size. Financials is not held, so no cap is breached.

triggers.text: TTM operating margin falls below 26%, under every year except the FY2023 trough (23.5%), showing regulation is compressing take rates structurally.
TTM ROIC falls below 14%, giving up most of the recovery from 10.0% in FY2023 to 18.5%, signalling the network moat is eroding.
TTM FCF margin falls below 28%, under the five-year FY range of 31.0%-44.3%, showing float outflows or lost volumes are draining cash generation.

Management withdraws or cuts the FY2026 EBITDA guidance or the 2027-2028 growth target in a results release, or a further country imposes a meal-voucher fee cap, or net debt/EBITDA on the ratios page rises above 2.5x.
